issues.issue_title: PKA ECC DoubleBaseLadder RAM offsets overlap inputs/outputs -> invalid secp256r1 point on STM32H7S3L8
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: PKA ECC DoubleBaseLadder RAM offsets overlap inputs/outputs -> invalid secp256r1 point on STM32H7S3L8
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7RS, mcu_series=H7, board=NUCLEO-H7S3L8, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=8
Root cause: ST Internal Reference: 6a0204153bc84f98a49f6547f4e45a3e Hello @Bruce-Copilot, Regarding the issue, we have tested an **ECC Double Base Ladder** example using the ECDSA test vectors downloaded from the NIST CAVP website, and it works as expected.
Fix: **Goal** I want to use mbedtls_ecdsa_genkey to accelerate the TLS handshake, but I can't implement this function on STM32.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, NUCLEO-H7S3L8, HAL, bug_report, high, bug, internal bug tracker, pka, mbedtls_ecdsa_genkey, TLS, STM32, mbedtls_ecdsa_sign

Technical details:
**Goal** I want to use mbedtls_ecdsa_genkey to accelerate the TLS handshake, but I can't implement this function on STM32. However, I have successfully implemented mbedtls_ecdsa_sign and mbedtls_ecdsa_verify. I would like to confirm whether it is possible to generate a private key on the STM32H7S3L8? Don't worry about whether the example is based on Zephyr; it can be based on STMCubeiDE or any IDE. ### Environment - Target MCU: STM32H7S3L8 - Board: NUCLEO-H7S3L8 (Zephyr board: nucleo_h7s3l8, adjust if different) - Zephyr: (23892b038f6a94f6677318fecbc4df98fc8e2ac5) - hal_stm32: 9325b43737ffca79ffe1af6300c90ffde98919da https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/hal_stm32 - Crypto library: mbedTLS (Zephyr integrated) ### Summary When using STM32 PKA HAL ECC Double Base Ladder mode to compute Q = d*G on secp256r1, HAL_PKA_ECCDoubleBaseLadder() returns HAL_OK but the produced (X,Y) is not a valid secp256r1 public key point (mbedtls_ecp_check_pubkey fails). The HAL defines overlapping PKA RAM offsets for this mode: - input k overlaps output error - input m overlaps output X This makes correct computation impossible / results corrupted. Evidence (overlapping macros) From the STM32 PKA HAL (stm32h7rsxx_hal_pka.c or related private header), Double Base Ladder offsets: Inputs: #define PKA_ECC_DOUBLE_LADDER_IN_K_INTEGER ((0x0520UL - PKA_RAM_OFFSET)>>2) #define PKA_ECC_DOUBLE_LADDER_IN_M_INTEGER ((0x0578UL - PKA_RAM_OFFSET)>>2) Outputs: #define PKA_ECC_DOUBLE_LADDER_OUT_ERROR ((0x0520UL - PKA_RAM_OFFSET)>>2) #define PKA_ECC_DOUBLE_LADDER_OUT_RESULT_X ((0x0578UL - PKA_RAM_OFFSET)>>2) #define PKA_ECC_DOUBLE_LADDER_OUT_RESULT_Y ((0x05D0UL - PKA_RAM_OFFSET)>>2) Overlaps: - 0x0520 is both IN_K_INTEGER and OUT_ERROR - 0x0578 is both IN_M_INTEGER and OUT_RESULT_X ### Reproduction (minimal) 1. Use secp256r1 parameters (p, a=-3, b, Gx, Gy, n). 2. Generate random private key d in [1, n-1]. 3. Call HAL_PKA_ECCDoubleBaseLadder with: - modulusSize = 32, primeOrderSize = 32 - coefA = |a| = 3, coefSign = 1 (a = -3) - modulus = p - integerK = d (32 bytes, big-endian) - integerM = 0 (32 bytes, big-endian) - P1 = G with Z1 = 1 - P2 = G with Z2 = 1 (m=0 so P2 should not matter) 4. Read X/Y using HAL_PKA_ECCDoubleBaseLadder_GetResult(). 5. Load X/Y into mbedTLS point Q and run: ret = mbedtls_ecp_check_pubkey(&grp, &Q); Expected behavior - mbedtls_ecp_check_pubkey() returns 0 (Q is valid secp256r1 point) Actual behavior - HAL_PKA_ECCDoubleBaseLadder returns HAL_OK - mbedtls_ecp_check_pubkey() returns -19584 (invalid public key) - ECDSA verify with this public key fails accordingly. c #include <string.h> #include <zephyr/logging/log.h> LOG_MODULE_REGISTER(ecdsa_alt, LOG_LEVEL_DBG); #include <stm32h7rsxx_hal.h> #include <stm32h7rsxx_hal_pka.h> #include <mbedtls/ecdsa.h> #include <mbedtls/ecp.h> #include <mbedtls/bignum.h> #include <mbedtls/platform_util.h> /* mbedTLS 3.x compatibility */ #ifndef MBEDTLS_PRIVATE #define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member) member #endif #define ECDSA_CTX_GRP(ctx) ((ctx)->MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(grp)) #define ECDSA_CTX_D(ctx) ((ctx)->MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(d)) #define ECDSA_CTX_Q(ctx) ((ctx)->MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(Q)) #define ECP_POINT_X(P) ((P).MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(X)) #define ECP_POINT_Y(P) ((P).MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(Y)) #define ECP_POINT_Z(P) ((P).MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(Z)) /* Use a local error for "HW accel failed" (avoid abusing ALLOC_FAILED). */ #ifndef MBEDTLS_ERR_PLATFORM_HW_ACCEL_FAILED #define MBEDTLS_ERR_PLATFORM_HW_ACCEL_FAILED (-0x7F00) #endif /* secp256r1 constants (big-endian) */ static const uint8_t secp256r1_p[32] = { 0xff,0xff,0xff,0xff, 0x00,0x00,0x00,0x01, 0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00, 0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00, 0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00, 0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00, 0xff,0xff,0xff,0xff, 0xff,0xff,0xff,0xff }; /* |a| = 3 (a = -3) */ static const uint8_t secp256r1_a_abs[32] = { 0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00, 0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x03 }; static const uint8_t secp256r1_Gx[32] = { 0x6B,0x17,0xD1,0xF2,0xE1,0x2C,0x42,0x47,0xF8,0xBC,0xE6,0xE5,0x63,0xA4,0x40,0xF2, 0x77,0x03,0x7D,0x81,0x2D,0xEB,0x33,0xA0,0xF4,0xA1,0x39,0x45,0xD8,0x98,0xC2,0x96 }; static const uint8_t secp256r1_Gy[32] = { 0x4F,0xE3,0x42,0xE2,0xFE,0x1A,0x7F,0x9B,0x8E,0xE7,0xEB,0x4A,0x7C,0x0F,0x9E,0x16, 0x2B,0xCE,0x33,0x57,0x6B,0x31,0x5E,0xCE,0xCB,0xB6,0x40,0x68,0x37,0xBF,0x51,0xF5 }; /* Global PKA handle (simple blocking use) */ static PKA_HandleTypeDef hpka = { .Instance = PKA, .State = HAL_PKA_STATE_READY }; static int pka_inited; int mbedtls_ecdsa_genkey( mbedtls_ecdsa_context *ctx, mbedtls_ecp_group_id gid, int (*f_rng)(void *, unsigned char *, size_t), void *p_rng ) { int ret = 0; LOG_INF("genkey enter: gid=%d", (int)gid); if (ctx == NULL || f_rng == NULL) { LOG_ERR("genkey bad input"); return MBEDTLS_ERR_ECP_BAD_INPUT_DATA; } if (gid != MBEDTLS_ECP_DP_SECP256R1) { LOG_ERR("genkey unsupported curve gid=%d", (int)gid); return MBEDTLS_ERR_ECP_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE; } ret = mbedtls_ecp_group_load(&ECDSA_CTX_GRP(ctx), gid); if (ret != 0) { LOG_ERR("mbedtls_ecp_group_load ret=%d", ret); return ret; } uint8_t d_buf[32]; uint8_t x_out[32]; uint8_t y_out[32]; uint8_t qx_buf[32]; uint8_t qy_buf[32]; uint8_t zero32[32]; uint8_t one32[32]; mbedtls_mpi d_mpi; mbedtls_mpi_init(&d_mpi); memset(d_buf, 0, sizeof(d_buf)); memset(x_out, 0, sizeof(x_out)); memset(y_out, 0, sizeof(y_out)); memset(qx_buf, 0, sizeof(qx_buf)); memset(qy_buf, 0, sizeof(qy_buf)); memset(zero32, 0, sizeof(zero32)); memset(one32, 0, sizeof(one32)); one32[31] = 1; /* big-endian 1 */ /* Generate private key d in [1, N-1] */ for (unsigned attempt = 0; attempt < 100; attempt++) { ret = f_rng(p_rng, d_buf, sizeof(d_buf)); if (ret != 0) { LOG_ERR("f_rng failed"); ret = MBEDTLS_ERR_ECP_RANDOM_FAILED; goto cleanup; } ret = mbedtls_mpi_read_binary(&d_mpi, d_buf, sizeof(d_buf)); if (ret != 0) { goto cleanup; } if (mbedtls_mpi_cmp_int(&d_mpi, 0) == 0) { continue; } if (mbedtls_mpi_cmp_mpi(&d_mpi, &ECDSA_CTX_GRP(ctx).N) >= 0) { continue; } break; } if (mbedtls_mpi_cmp_int(&d_mpi, 0) == 0 || mbedtls_mpi_cmp_mpi(&d_mpi, &ECDSA_CTX_GRP(ctx).N) >= 0) { LOG_ERR("failed to generate valid private key d"); ret = MBEDTLS_ERR_ECP_RANDOM_FAILED; goto cleanup; } /* Hardware: Q = d*G using DoubleBaseLadder: R = k*P1 + m*P2 with m=0 */ { PKA_ECCDoubleBaseLadderInTypeDef in; PKA_ECCDoubleBaseLadderOutTypeDef out; memset(&in, 0, sizeof(in)); memset(&out, 0, sizeof(out)); in.primeOrderSize = 32; in.modulusSize = 32; /* P-256: a = -3 => coefSign=1, |a|=3 */ in.coefSign = 1; in.coefA = secp256r1_a_abs; in.modulus = secp256r1_p; in.integerK = d_buf; in.integerM = zero32; in.basePointX1 = secp256r1_Gx; in.basePointY1 = secp256r1_Gy; in.basePointZ1 = one32; /* P2 doesn't matter when m=0 */ in.basePointX2 = secp256r1_Gx; in.basePointY2 = secp256r1_Gy; in.basePointZ2 = one32; out.ptX = x_out; out.ptY = y_out; LOG_DBG("calling HAL_PKA_ECCDoubleBaseLadder (Q=d*G)..."); if (HAL_PKA_ECCDoubleBaseLadder(&hpka, &in, 5000) != HAL_OK) { uint32_t he = HAL_PKA_GetError(&hpka); LOG_ERR("HAL_PKA_ECCDoubleBaseLadder failed: hal_err=0x%08x state=%d CR=0x%08x SR=0x%08x", (unsigned)he, (int)HAL_PKA_GetState(&hpka), (unsigned)hpka.Instance->CR, (unsigned)hpka.Instance->SR); ret = MBEDTLS_ERR_PLATFORM_HW_ACCEL_FAILED; goto cleanup; } HAL_PKA_ECCDoubleBaseLadder_GetResult(&hpka, &out); memcpy(qx_buf, x_out, 32); memcpy(qy_buf, y_out, 32); } /* Write key into ctx */ ret = mbedtls_mpi_read_binary(&ECDSA_CTX_D(ctx), d_buf, sizeof(d_buf)); if (ret != 0) { goto cleanup; } ret = mbedtls_mpi_read_binary(&ECP_POINT_X(ECDSA_CTX_Q(ctx)), qx_buf, sizeof(qx_buf)); if (ret != 0) { goto cleanup; } ret = mbedtls_mpi_read_binary(&ECP_POINT_Y(ECDSA_CTX_Q(ctx)), qy_buf, sizeof(qy_buf)); if (ret != 0) { goto cleanup; } ret = mbedtls_mpi_lset(&ECP_POINT_Z(ECDSA_CTX_Q(ctx)), 1); if (ret != 0) { goto cleanup; } /* These two logs match your sample output */ ret = mbedtls_ecp_check_pubkey(&ECDSA_CTX_GRP(ctx), &ECDSA_CTX_Q(ctx)); LOG_INF("mbedtls_ecp_check_pubkey ret=%d", ret); if (ret != 0) { LOG_ERR("generated public key is invalid for P-256"); goto cleanup; } LOG_INF("genkey ok (double-base ladder)"); ret = 0; cleanup: mbedtls_platform_zeroize(d_buf, sizeof(d_buf)); mbedtls_platform_zeroize(qx_buf, sizeof(qx_buf)); mbedtls_platform_zeroize(qy_buf, sizeof(qy_buf)); mbedtls_mpi_free(&d_mpi); return ret; } ### Example logs [00:00:06.316,000] <inf> ecdsa: . Seeding the random number generator... [00:00:06.330,000] <inf> ecdsa: ok . Generating key pair... [00:00:06.336,000] <inf> ecdsa_alt: PKA init: starting [00:00:06.342,000] <inf> ecdsa_alt: PKA init: done (CR=0x00000001 SR=0x00000001) [00:00:06.350,000] <inf> ecdsa_alt: genkey enter: gid=3 [00:00:06.356,000] <dbg> ecdsa_alt: mbedtls_ecdsa_genkey: calling HAL_PKA_ECCDoubleBaseLadder (Q=d*G)... [00:00:06.377,000] <inf> ecdsa_alt: mbedtls_ecp_check_pubkey ret=-19584 [00:00:06.384,000] <err> ecdsa_alt: generated public key is invalid for P-256 [00:00:06.392,000] <inf> ecdsa: failed ! mbedtls_ecdsa_genkey returned -19584 **Additional observations** - HAL_PKA_ECDSASign / HAL_PKA_ECDSAVerif works correctly for secp256r1 on the same target. - HAL_PKA_PointCheck reports IsOnCurve=0 even for the known base point G, and HAL_PKA_ECCMulEx returns OPERR, which may indicate broader ECC mode RAM layout mismatch on this target. **Request** Please confirm whether the stm32h7rsxx HAL PKA ECC mode RAM layouts are correct for STM32H7S3 series. If not, please provide corrected offsets / updated HAL driver so ECC point multiplication (key generation/ECDH) can be hardware-accelerated on STM32H7S3 devices.

Key comments:
ST Internal Reference: 6a0204153bc84f98a49f6547f4e45a3e Hello @Bruce-Copilot, Regarding the issue, we have tested an **ECC Double Base Ladder** example using the ECDSA test vectors downloaded from the NIST CAVP website, and it works as expected. Using the same input values for d, Qx, and Qy from the NIST **KeyPair.rsp** file, we were able to successfully generate the corresponding public key values, which confirms that the implementation is functioning correctly for this case. For reference, the verified example was: Private Key: d = b1e79339d02a6c0331b057b2e84fb93a2648341d7c891f3e46591cdb6200a805 Public Key: Qx = 52c61281593ad5ecf8d041f778dd97777f9cd89e9e4830015de52052e2cd0778 Qy = 2ac533912f66d98c0009e4cd494c9094637555699ab93902cd3b457eff09d923 The test vectors were taken from the NIST Cryptographic Algorithm Validation Program (CAVP) digital signature test vectors, available here: https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cryptographic-algorithm-validation-program/digital-signatures So could you show me your code? I'm confused about these parameters and don't know how to fill them in. I've tried using AI many times, but without success. For example, what should 'd' be assign

Problem: NUCLEO-H7S3L8 - Reference to nonexistent header in USB device example projects
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7RS, mcu_series=H7, board=NUCLEO-H7S3L8, component=USB, layer=Middleware, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=low, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=7
Root cause: Hi @b4shful, Thank you for the heads-up.
Fix: Many of the projects in Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/USB_Device have READMEs referring to "Header JP4" This header does not exist whatsoever on the board, it is not anywhere in the schematics (MB1737 NUCLEO-H7S3L8) or the User Manual UM3276.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, NUCLEO-H7S3L8, Middleware, USB, bug_report, low, bug, projects, internal bug tracker, usb-pd, USB_Device, JP4

Technical details:
Many of the projects in Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/USB_Device have READMEs referring to "Header JP4" This header does not exist whatsoever on the board, it is not anywhere in the schematics (MB1737 NUCLEO-H7S3L8) or the User Manual UM3276. CDC_Standalone https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7RS/tree/main/Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/USB_Device/CDC_Standalone ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90264872-1e10-4084-9a53-1562a31e2990) Composite_CDC_HID_Standalone https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7RS/tree/main/Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/USB_Device/Composite_CDC_HID_Standalone ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0af09b4e-6776-437b-8432-25a3a28f81f9) HID_Standalone https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7RS/tree/main/Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/USB_Device/HID_Standalone ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3e08612f-0541-427d-b49f-4b176dcf9b8f) Video_Standalone https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7RS/tree/main/Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/USB_Device/Video_Standalone ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49319019-d7e9-4205-85c2-d54111fd95de) What header on the NUCLEO-H7S3L8 is this actually referring to? Potentially the UCPD option on power selector JP3?

Key comments:
Hi @b4shful, Thank you for the heads-up. Indeed, looks like a typo as there is no mention of any JP4 in the board's [manual](https://www.st.com/resource/en/user_manual/um3276-stm32h7rx7sx-nucleo144-board-mb1737-stmicroelectronics.pdf). I'll let our development teams know about this in order to correct the typo. ST Internal Reference: 208397 Hi @b4shful, I hope you are fine. It has been confirmed that the mention of JP4 should be replaced by JP3, as you guessed. We'll try to have these README.md files corrected. issues.issue_title: LwIP_HTTP_Server_Raw Triggers MPU HardFault on NUCLEO-H7S3L8
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: LwIP_HTTP_Server_Raw Triggers MPU HardFault on NUCLEO-H7S3L8
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7RS, mcu_series=H7, board=NUCLEO-H7S3L8, component=None, layer=Middleware, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=6
Root cause: I've found a solution by manually modifying the DTCM_AXI_SHARE Option Byte in CubeProgrammer.
Fix: Hello, I am working with a [NUCLEO-H7S3L8](https://www.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, NUCLEO-H7S3L8, Middleware, bug_report, high, bug, invalid, projects, eth, STM32-H7S3L8H6U, LwIP_HTTP_Server_Raw, MPU

Technical details:
Hello, I am working with a [NUCLEO-H7S3L8](https://www.st.com/en/evaluation-tools/nucleo-h7s3l8.html) (STM32-H7S3L8H6U). When debugging the Application located at [Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/LwIP/LwIP_HTTP_Server_Raw](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7RS/tree/main/Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/LwIP/LwIP_HTTP_Server_Raw) , the MPU appears to trigger a HardFault Handler during LWIP initialization. Stack Trace: > Thread #1 [main] 1 [core: 1] (Suspended : Signal : SIGTRAP:Trace/breakpoint trap) > HardFault_Handler() at stm32h7rsxx_it.c:85 0x70001874 > <signal handler called>() at 0xffffffe9 > ptr_to_mem() at mem.c:452 0x7000bfb4 > mem_init() at mem.c:531 0x7000c16e > lwip_init() at init.c:349 0x7000ac22 > MX_LWIP_Init() at lwip.c:281 0x7000128e > main() at main.c:125 0x70001470 > Reset_Handler() at startup_stm32h7s3l8hx.s:97 0x700006e6 [IMAGE ATTACHED] This application is set up to run as described in the Application's [README](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7RS/blob/main/Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/LwIP/LwIP_HTTP_Server_Raw/README.md) where the XIP_Boot is loaded prior to the Appli in the Debug Configuration [IMAGE ATTACHED] The HardFault occurs when LWIP is attempting to calculate/access the end of the LWIP_RAM_HEAP at address 0x2404_3800. [IMAGE ATTACHED] I've checked the MPU configuration in the [project's IOC file](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7RS/blob/main/Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/LwIP/LwIP_HTTP_Server_Raw/LwIP_HTTP_Server_Raw.ioc), and it appears to cover the correct range, starting at address 0x2404_0000 and extending 16KB (well past 0x2404_3800) [IMAGE ATTACHED] This address space appears to be located within AXI SRAM3. Perhaps I am missing a configuration to enable the AXI bus? [IMAGE ATTACHED] If there is a configuration fix that I am missing, I am all ears. Much appreciated!

Key comments:
I've found a solution by manually modifying the DTCM_AXI_SHARE Option Byte in CubeProgrammer. The hard fault no longer occurs. I'm unsure if the board shipped with this Option Byte set to 2, or if I changed it during experimentation myself. - DTCM_AXI_SHARE should be set to 0 or 3 to set a DTCM value of 64KB. My value was originally set to 2, implying an extended DTCM size from 64KB to 192 KB. I believe this allowed the DTCM to extend into SRAM3, preventing the read/write to the SRAM3 region, resulting in a failure when allocation the LWIP_RAM_HEAP. [IMAGE ATTACHED] Inspecting the Block Diagram showed that SRAM3 can be "shared DTCM". [IMAGE ATTACHED] On page 159 of this document (https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0477-stm32h7rx7sx-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf) it I found this option byte described. [IMAGE ATTACHED] Adding this option byte to the [README's User Option Bytes requirement](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7RS/blob/ea9d5c08521dc1918ac804b6079e8530f0746f49/Projects/NUCLEO-H7S3L8/Applications/LwIP/LwIP_HTTP_Server_Raw/README.md?plain=1#L64C5-L64C34) may be beneficial for other developers Hello @rneureuther1, Thank you f

issues.issue_title: Adresses of SAI1 and SAI2 in CMSIS file is swapped
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Adresses of SAI1 and SAI2 in CMSIS file is swapped
Context: repo=STM32CubeH7RS, mcu_series=H7, board=NUCLEO-H7S3L8, component=None, layer=CubeMX, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=5
Root cause: ST Internal Reference: 189421 Hello @Protoxy22, It appears that the issue is related to the CMSIS File not .
Fix: Hi, I have a NUCLEO-H7S3L8 and I think there is an addresses mistake in the .
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, NUCLEO-H7S3L8, CubeMX, bug_report, medium, bug, internal bug tracker, cmsis, sai, SAI1_A, SAI1_B, SFR

Technical details:
Hi, I have a NUCLEO-H7S3L8 and I think there is an addresses mistake in the .svd files and potentially other hardware description files. You can reproduce and see the mistake if you setup the SAI1_A and SAI1_B on CubeMX, generate the code and debug the program, you will see in the SFR widget of STM32CubeIDE (the .svd file) that it's the SAI2 registers configured instead. It also affects the CubeMX configuration of SAI, we can't set SAI1_A on Master and SAI1_B on Slave synchronous which is very annoying (image below) I'm not sure if it's the right place to report this, but I would really appreciate if you follow this issue on the right ST team. Thanks. ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e368e73-903f-49b3-b66e-c7cc58aabfde)

Key comments:
ST Internal Reference: 189421 Hello @Protoxy22, It appears that the issue is related to the CMSIS File not .svd file. With regards. > Hello @Protoxy22, > > It appears that the issue is related to the CMSIS File not .svd file. > > With regards. Hi, ok I'm glad you have made progress on this Thanks Hello @Protoxy22, I hope you're doing well. After further investigation, we found out that the mistake was indeed on **svd** file and the [RM0477](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0477-stm32h7rx7sx-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf), section 2.3.2 Memory map and register boundary addresses. The RM has been recently updated. The fix for the SVD file, it will be available in the next release of CUBEIDE and other IDEs. Thank you again, please allow me to close the issue.
